title: Geo concurrent write window: graceful traffic bisection and customer rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers and a subset of Hosted traffic experienced elevated 5xx errors and write anomalies during an automated capacity rebalance across regions. Root cause appears to be a narrow concurrent-write window in the leader-lease renewal path that allowed two region leaders to accept conflicting writes for a short interval during cross-region traffic steering. This ticket coordinates an urgent short-term traffic bisection mitigations plan, a targeted bugfix for leader-lease renewal, customer rollback sequencing, and post-incident follow-ups to avoid recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy canary that simulates leader-lease renewal latency by introducing 100-300ms sleep before lease refresh in region A.
2) Initiate cross-region gradual traffic shift (25%->75%) while performing KV metadata sync with 30s snapshot interval.
3) Run concurrent write workload from 10 tenants performing parallel small updates (100qps each) targeted at the same shard.
4) Observe transient duplicate-success responses and 5xx spikes in telemetry between t+18s and t+42s.
current_mitigation:
- Activated graceful traffic bisection: traffic steering policy updated to split affected tenant traffic 60/40 instead of full cutover.
- Temporarily disabled non-critical background KV compactions on Dedicated pools to reduce lease renewal jitter.
- Applied emergency rate limit on write-heavy tenants (per-tenant throttling) to keep cluster within predictable window.
- Coordinated with on-call SRE to enable verbose lease/term logs and increased metric resolution for leader changes.
- Created temporary tenant routing exception for one enterprise customer to route to warm-standby region until resync completes.
short_term_plan:
1) Finish rollout of traffic bisection policy across edge routers with 1-minute health-checks and automatic rollback if 5xx > 1% for 5m.
2) Patch leader-lease renewal to add an idempotent preflight (check-and-prepare) and fast-fail on version mismatch (hotfix branch runtime/lease-hotfix-834210).
3) Run a controlled canary of the hotfix on two small tenants in Dedicated, monitor KV convergence and 5xx.
4) For affected customers, offer data-consistency assessment and coordinate snapshot resync where necessary.
long_term_fix:
- Replace current lease renewal RPC with a two-phase renewal that serializes leadership handoff across regions and guarantees a quiescent checkpoint window.
- Add per-tenant write quiescing API allowing a fast customer-level drain before cross-region moves.
- Expand observability: add a 'lease_conflict' signal and a dedicated dashboard for cross-region write anomalies.
- Update rollout playbooks to include mandatory 5m shadow mode for any >30% traffic migration between regions.
qa_plan:
- Run fuzzed cross-region tests that randomly delay lease RPCs and assert no dual-leader acceptance for any shard.
- Add integration test that simulates production traffic patterns (mix of reads/embeds/writes) at peak RPS.
- Validation checklist: no duplicate write confirmations, no unacknowledged conflicting writes, no 5xx spikes >0.5% for 30 minutes post-rollout.
monitoring_checks:
- Add temporary alerts: KV.Lease.Conflicts >= 1 over 1m, RegionSwitch.5xxRate > 0.8% for 5m, Tenant.WriteThrottleRate > 5% sustained.
- Dashboards to watch: per-region leader changes, lease_refresh_latency_p50/p95, per-tenant write success rate, redispatch queue length.
- Post-fix: verify rollback triggers and canary metrics for 2 hours after each rollout stage.
